decisions.rationale: "melanoma" in "in a human melanoma" names a single specific disease (melanoma) used as the head of the phrase, not as a modifier, so it is annotated as SpecificDisease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate 1 (organism 'human' excluded)

decisions.rationale: "tumor" in "tumor-specific antigen" is used as a modifier of the noun "antigen"; 'tumor' is retained as a disease term but is annotated as a Modifier here.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers); What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: "melanoma" in the second sentence "in a human melanoma" refers to the specific disease, so it is annotated as SpecificDisease; duplicate mentions are annotated separately.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: "melanoma" in "autologous cultured melanoma cells" modifies the noun "cells", so it is annotated as a Modifier.
"metastasis" refers to a biological process (spread of tumor) and describes tissue origin rather than naming a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5 (references to biological processes)

decisions.rationale: "melanoma" in "one additional melanoma among 28" refers to the specific disease as the head noun of the phrase, so it is annotated as SpecificDisease.
"melanomas" in "28 melanomas analyzed" is the plural head noun referring to cases of the specific disease melanoma, so it is annotated as SpecificDisease.
"tumor" in "tumor-specific antigen" modifies the noun "antigen" in this sentence, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers); What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: "tumor" in "tumor suppressor p16INK4a" modifies the noun "suppressor" and names a gene class rather than a disease, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers); What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer and tumor are retained)
